chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from one of our companions, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Muhammad ibn Atiyya, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, chose for His prophets farming and agriculture, so that they might not dislike anything from the drops of the sky.'
ai.seo_question: Why did Allah choose farming for the prophets?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the divine wisdom behind selecting agriculture for the prophets, highlighting how engaging with the earth fosters a holistic acceptance of natural cycles, including rain and drought. This perspective underscores the Shia scholarly view that prophetic livelihoods were designed to cultivate humility and gratitude, preventing disdain for any aspect of God's creation. The emphasis on 'harvest and sowing' reflects the spiritual dignity of labor as a means of sustaining both physical needs and spiritual connection with the Creator.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from one of our companions, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, form Muhammad Bin Atiyya who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying, ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Chose the farming and the agriculture for His<sup>azwj</sup> Prophets<sup>as</sup>, lest they<sup>as</sup> dislike something from the drops (falling) from the sky’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from certain persons of his people from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Muhammad ibn ‘Atiyyah who has said the following: “

I heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has chosen farming and plantation for His prophets so that they will not dislike the drops falling from the sky.”’
